meta.title: Verified rules layer
meta.purpose: The rules that convert raw reporting into decision-grade availability information. Only rules confirmed against an official NFL page are marked verified. Anything unconfirmed is left blank and flagged.
meta.seasons_confirmed: Rules confirmed as published; see per-rule 'as_of' for when the league announced them. Whether each rule is still in force for the 2026 season is stated per rule and flagged where it could not be confirmed.

rules.statement: The Practice Report lists an injured player in exactly one of three categories: Did Not Participate, Limited Participation, or Full Participation.
rules.definitions: Limited Participation = less than 100 percent of the player's normal repetitions. Full Participation = 100 percent of normal repetitions.

rules.statement: The Game Status Report uses three designations: Out, Doubtful, Questionable.
rules.definitions: Out = the player will not play. Doubtful = it is unlikely the player will participate. Questionable = it is uncertain whether the player will play.

rules.statement: The 'Probable' game status no longer exists.
rules.definitions: Eliminated because approximately 95 percent of players listed as Probable in prior years did in fact play.

rules.statement: A player certain to play is not listed on the Game Status Report even if he appeared on that week's practice report. If such a player is then deactivated, the club must explain to the league and is subject to discipline.
The deadline for publishing the Game Status Report.
rules.note: A commonly repeated figure (4:00 p.m. ET two days before kickoff, with Thursday games on Wednesday) appeared only in secondary reporting that was not fetched and not published by the NFL. Left blank. See F-02.

rules.statement: A player placed on reserve/injured becomes eligible to return once four games have elapsed since the date he was placed on the list.
Eight players per season may be designated to return from reserve/injured and/or reserve/non-football injury/illness to the 53-man active roster or the practice squad.
rules.definitions: Each return designation counts against the club's allotment of eight.

rules.statement: An individual player may return from reserve/injured a maximum of twice per season.
rules.definitions: Each return counts against the eight designations.

rules.statement: Practice squads were increased to 16 players.
rules.definitions: Up from 14 under the prior rules.
rules.conflict: A 2026 Associated Press article surfaced in search describes 17-man practice squads. That page was not fetched and the NFL has not been re-checked for the current size. See I-06 / F-02.

rules.statement: A practice-squad player may be elevated to the game-day roster a maximum of three times per season.

rules.note: '53' is universally repeated but was not confirmed on an official NFL page during this session. Left blank rather than filled from memory or from a non-official article. See F-02.
Not confirmed on an official page during this session. Left blank. See F-02.

rules.statement: NFL.com club roster pages expose a per-player roster-status flag; the value 'ACT' (active) was observed for every listed player on the Washington Commanders page.
NFL.com club roster pages do not publish a depth order (1st / 2nd / 3rd string) column.
rules.note: This is the single most important finding for the backup/deficiency requirement: the official roster feed gives position and roster status, not the depth chart order.

rules.statement: 2026 rule changes listed by NFL Football Operations.
rules.definitions: 6-1-3 alignment requirements for receiving-team players in the setup zone on a kickoff or safety kick; 6-1-5 dead-ball spot after a touchback when the kickoff is from the 50-yard line; 6-1-6 kicking team may declare an onside kick at any time; 19-2 league personnel may consult on-field officials on potential disqualification for flagrant football and non-football acts even if not called on the field.

official_page_absent.claim: An NFL-authored point spread / total / price page
official_page_absent.conclusion: No NFL-published odds page exists at that path. Narrower and more accurate statement, confirmed by S13: NFL widgets display odds supplied by partner bookmakers (FanDuel, Caesars, DraftKings) and redirect to the bookmaker. The league does not author, archive or publish lines of its own.
